checks.fact: Title plan must be read with the register.
Title plan is one element of a registered title alongside the register and filed documents.
Title plan identifies the general extent of registered land.
All title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary has been determined.
Title plans are based on Ordnance Survey mapping.
The OS mapping edition current at registration is used.
Adjoining title plans can therefore be based on different OS mapping editions.
Urban title plans are usually prepared at 1:1250.
Rural title plans are usually prepared at 1:2500.
Large rural title plans may be 1:5000 or 1:10000.
Red edging generally follows the inside of the boundary line.
Dimensions shown on older title plans do not convert a general boundary into an exact boundary.
The physical reference point used by an old dimension may have disappeared or changed.
Title-plan dimensions are no longer routinely reproduced.

promotion_rule: Exact revision 14 runtime output plus remote integrity readback is required before promoting any parcel height-difference value.
